To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
InxGa1-xAs-based ohmic contact for p-type GaAS has been developed by RF-sputtering.
InxGa1-xAs-based ohmic contact which showed excellent contact property for n-GaAS was demonstrated to be applicable for p-GaAs.
the contact resistance of the InxGa 1-xAs-based ohmic contact for p-GaAs is low, and it is stable at high temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation of InxGa 1−xAs (0.15 < x < 0.35) ohmic contacts on both n and p-type GaAs substrates by radio-frequency magnetron sputtering.
the development of a new ohmic contact technology for both n andp-GaAs, which is based on radio-frequency sputtered InxGa1-xAs.
the development of InxGa 1−xAs ohmic contacts for n-GaAS by radio-frequency sutureing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present experiment showed that InxGa1-xAs-based ohmic contact can be applied to p-GaAS ohmic contact as well as to n-GaAs.
the InxGa 1−xAs ohmic contacts prepared by radio frequency sputtering are very promising for practical application.
radio-frequency sputtered InxGa1-xAs-based ohmic contact for p-GaAs is an attractive alternative to conventional ohmic contact for both n and/or p-GaAs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the InxGa 1−xAs alloy system is a very attractive material for ohmic contact to GaAs.
InxGa1-xAs is a very good candidate as an ohmic contact material.
the InxGa 1−xAs/GaAs superlattice (SL) is the best candidate for a contact layer in the Inx Ga1−xAs ohmic contact for both n and/or p-GaAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have demonstrated a new approach to the development of InGaAs-based ohmic contact technology for GaAs-based electronic devices.

the use of InxGa 1−xAs layers with high In content is very effective for the preparation of low resistance ohmic contacts for n-GaAS and p-GaAS, and that the use of radio-frequency sputter deposition is very effective in preparing InxGa1xAs layers with a high degree of uniformity.
InxGa1-xAs-based ohmic contact which showed excellent contact property for n-GaAS can be applicable to p-type GaAs.
